Commentary.Commentary: We are back, folks! The Indian boys are in a huddle before heading out and taking their positions. Campbell Kellaway and Teague Wyllie walk out to bat. Rajvardhan Hangargekar will start with the first new ball. Here we go...
... CHASE TIME ...

Right then. To chase 291 in a semi-final will take a lot of application from the Aussie batters. Plus, the pitch seems to have some help for the new-ball bowlers so the openers of Australia Under-19 will need to bat really well. They do have a good batting department but they rely heavily on the top three. This could be an interesting chase if they get a good start. Do join us in a short while for the chase.

The head coach of India Under-19, Hrishikesh Kanitkar comes up for a chat. He says that it was a very spaced innings, initially, they were cautious as the wicket had something in it for the bowlers and at the right time they accelerated. Reckons that it's a good score but they're only halfway there. Adds that Yash Dhull is a very mature player, has a lot of shots and he is a complete package. Informs that Dhull is working on playing through full overs. Praises Shaik Rasheed as well and tells that they combined really well and were an effective and potent pair. Regarding India's bowling plans, Kanitkar replies that they will stick to hard lines and try to attack as well as wickets make a huge difference. Feels that you have to take it as it comes and admits that Australia have a very good batting line-up as well.

Now, good teams look to double the score that they have at the 30-over mark. India Under-19 had two set batters at the crease and the stage was set for them to tee off. Dhull and Rasheed got to their fifties and started to smack the ball all over the ground. The Aussies were under a lot of pressure and they bowled a lot of loose deliveries. They also missed a run out chance of Dhull which hurt them a lot. Dhull got a hundred but his wicket and that of Rasheed, who fell on 94, on consecutive deliveries gave the Australian camp a bit of hope. But those hopes were shattered as India Under-19 got 49 in the last 4 overs after losing their set batters. Jack Nisbet and William Salzmann were the only two wicket-takers as the rest of the Aussie bowlers had a tough day. Fair to say that the first half of the game belonged to the Indian boys.

The Australia Under-19 bowlers were brilliant with the new balls. They bowled in the right channels and there was rarely a loose delivery inside Powerplay 1. They had to wait a bit for the first wicket but had India Under-19 at 34-1 at the 10-over mark. The Indian team lost their other opener and were 37 for 2 with the run rate crawling under the radar. Yash Dhull and Shaik Rasheed were at the crease with a job to do. There was never any urgency to score quick runs as they rotated the strike and punished the loose deliveries to get them to 114 for 2 at the 30-over mark. Lachlan Shaw dropped the catch of Rasheed when he was on 24 and it cost them big.

What a finish for India Under-19! They lost a couple of wickets cheaply but after that, it was a brilliant show by the Indian boys! They scored 176 in the last 20 overs, of which, 108 came in the last 10. A smashing finish.

SIX! What a way to finish! Tom Whitney has served it in a platter, full and around off, Bana clears his front leg and pumps it over mid-wicket. The fielder near the fence is a mere spectator as it flies over his head. 27 from the final over and a 4-ball 20 from Dinesh Bana has propelled India Under-19 to 290/5!

FOUR! It's raining boundaries. Fuller and wider outside off, Dinesh Bana goes hard at it and ends up dragging it off the inner edge. It beats the stumps and scoots wide of short fine leg for a boundary.
SIX! High and handsome! Dinesh Bana has scored 10 runs off 2 balls. It's on a length and outside off, Bana lines himself and belts it down the ground over long on.
Very full and sharp, around leg from 'round the wicket, Nishant Sindhu fails to flick and it deflects off his boot to point for a leg bye.

SIX! This one has gone all the way! Fine leg dropped back before this ball but it doesn't matter. Short again, around middle, Nishant Sindhu rides the bounce and pulls it over fine leg for a biggie. Went with the wind and found the desired result.

FOUR! A good start to the last over for India Under-19. Whitney digs in a short ball around middle with fine leg up, Sindhu top-edges his pulls shot behind the fielder at short 45 and bags a boundary.
Tom Whitney (8-0-48-0) is set to bowl the final over. Quite strange that Jack Nisbet will not finish his 10 overs. He certainly has been the pick of the bowlers.
FOUR! Slower one has gone wrong. It's short and around leg, Dinesh Bana shuffles across the stumps and pulls it down to fine leg for a boundary.
Dinesh Bana walks out to bat.

OUT! TIMBER! This is very impressive death bowling by William Salzmann. Pacy yorker, around middle and leg at 135 kph, Rajvardhan Hangargekar swings his bat at it but fails to keep it out. It hits the base of the leg stump and the bails come off. Not much fireworks from the bat of Rajvardhan.
Very full and outside off, Sindhu drives it to the fielder at the edge of the circle at extra cover. Only a run.
Back of a length, around off and slower in pace, Rajvardhan drags his heave down to long on for a run.
This is clever bowling. Mixing it up well. Goes short and around off, Rajvardhan Hangargekar tries to slam it over the off side but misses again.
Deceived. Slower one, short and around off, Rajvardhan Hangargekar is way too early into the swing of his bat and misses.
Misses out! A low full toss, on middle. This is heaved off the inner half towards square leg for one. 15 from the over.
Length and wide outside off. Rajvardhan Hangargekar looks to carve it over covers but misses. Wide called.

SIX! High and handsome! A length ball, in the slot. Rajvardhan Hangargekar clears his front leg and sends the ball sailing straight back over the bowler's head. A huge hit and this brings up the 250 for India Under-19.

Well bowled. Slower ball, outside off. Sindhu goes for the heave but gets it away off the bottom edge. The ball rolls to cover. They take a single and the umpire has a word with Sindhu about running onto the danger area.
A nice bumper, around leg. Sindhu ducks under it and hopes that it will be called a wide but it isn't.
A slow full toss, on middle. Rajvardhan Hangargekar toe-ends his heave to long on for one.
Length and way outside off. Left alone and called a wide.
FOUR! Sliced away! Rajvardhan Hangargekar gets going now! Length ball, outside. He slices it over covers. The man in the deep runs to his right but cannot get there.

What was that? The batter could have played three shots, that delivery was so slow. Short and around off, taking ages to arrive. Nishant fails to decide what to do with it. Eventually, the ball on its own takes the outer half of his bat and rolls to short third man. What an exceptional over, just one from it!
A wide yorker outside off, Nishant again fails to keep it out. Going too hard.
Another miss! Full and slow, wide outside off, Sindhu tries to force it through the line but misses.
Beaten! Full and wide outside off, Sindhu tries to drive but misses.

Angling in from a length around leg, Rajvardhan Hangargekar tries to heave but misses. There is some sound and the keeper appeals but nothing from the umpire. The batters cross and it's given as a leg bye.
Sharp short delivery, Rajvardhan Hangargekar tries to pull but misses.
Nishant Sindhu walks out to bat. Also, William Salzmann (8-0-51-1) is back on.

OUT! CAUGHT! The replays are not conclusive. Short in length and wide outside off, Rasheed camps back and plays a full-blooded square cut through the line. It's aerial and the fielder inside the circle at backward point goes down to take a low catch. Jack Sinfield is claiming it and the batter starts to walk. But the two umpires want to get it checked. The soft signal is out. The third umpire watches a few replays. Very difficult to tell here. The ground slopes downwards in Antigua, so the angle is quite narrow. We are waiting for the decision. Nothing conclusive to overturn the on-field soft signal. So it will remain out. Rasheed misses his hundred and Australia Under-19 have an opportunity to limit the damage in the end overs.
Commentary.Howout: c Jack Sinfield b Jack Nisbet

Commentary.Commentary: Is that a clean catch? The soft signal is OUT as the TV umpire is called in. The first two angles are not very clear and it will be a very tough call. The TV umpire decides that there is not enough to overturn the soft signal and Shaik Rasheed has to walk back.
Who will replace Yash Dhull in the middle? In walks Rajvardhan Hangargekar. We could see some more fireworks here.

OUT! An unfortunate run out for the Indian skipper and it seems that was the only way Australia would have broken this partnership. Fuller in length and around off, Shaik Rasheed leans forward and drives it straight back. Jack Nisbet goes down low in his follow-through and gets some touch on the ball as it goes on to disturb the stumps at the non-striker's end. Yash Dhull has backed up too much and is well outside the crease. He trudges back but not before scoring a quality hundred.
Fuller and wider outside off, Dhull strokes it past the diving extra cover fielder for a run.
Fullish and on off, flicked to deep mid-wicket for a single.

Tom Whitney avoids embarrassment. Jack Nisbet senses the charge and bowls a full toss wide outside off, Yash throws his bat at it and it goes flying off the toe end of his bat. Tom Whitney at third man makes a near mess as he fumbles but then recovers to stop the ball. Only a run in the end.
Short and outside off, cut to point for a single.
A full toss, whipped to deep mid-wicket for a brace. The 200-run stand comes up!

SIX! Out of here! Menacing signs for Australia Under-19!​ Tom Whitney goes short and around off, Dhull gives the charge, loses his shape a bit but still manages to muscle it over wide long on for a biggie.

HUNDRED FOR YASH DHULL! He jumps in delight and the Indian dressing room is on its feet. What a quality knock from the skipper! Becomes only the third Indian captain to score a century in the ICC U-19 World Cup after Unmukt Chand and Virat Kohli! Back of a length, around off, Dhull shuffles across and gently works it in the gap at mid-wicket for a couple of runs. Can he finish the innings with a bang?

FOUR! Even better! Yash Dhull moves to 98. Short and close to off, Dhull steps back to make room, knows where the fielders are and powers it over backward point. Very skillful and smart from the Indian captain!

FOUR! Yash loves his shots square of the wicket. Tom Whitney serves it short and wide outside off, Dhull brings his wrists into play as he opens the face of his bat slightly and crunches it behind point.
Starts with a short ball around off, Rasheed dabs it down to backward point and scampers across to the other end.
Tom Whitney is back on. 7-0-29-0 for him so far and he needs to pick a wicket here.
Fuller in length and wide outside off, Yash cracks his drive to deep cover. The fielder runs across to his left to make the stop and they get two. 10 from the over!
A near-yorker, wide outside off, Shaik keeps it out in the gap at covers for one.
Rajvardhan Hangargekar is swinging his blade inside the dressing room. Could he be promoted up the order here? For that to happen though, one of these batters needs to get out first.

SIX! Thats' dismissed! No real follow-through of the bat, very punchy from Shaik. Too full in length, around middle and off, Rasheed shows the full face of the bat and launches it over long on. Moves to 90.
Jack Nisbet is playing with fire. Delivers yet another short and wide ball and gets away with it. Shaik Rasheed tries to cut but misses.
Play and a miss! Another short delivery wide outside off, Rasheed swishes and misses.
Short and wide outside off, could have been a wide but Yash Dhull chases as he falls down. It takes the bottom half of his bat and runs down to third man. They cross.
Change. Jack Nisbet (6-1-12-1) is back on.

Slower again, short and outside off, it takes ages to arrive and Yash waits for it patiently. Once it comes in his half, he swats it down to long off. Only a run. A good comeback over by William Salzmann.
Digs it short and around off, Rasheed pulls it across the line, not much timing and it goes towards the mid-wicket region. It's stopped inside the ring and they cross for a run.
Swing and a miss! Slower one, short and wide outside off, Shaik Rasheed is early into the pull shot and misses.
Width there, outside off, Yash glides it down to third man and rotates the strike.
Two dots. Short again, outside off, cut from the back foot but straight to point.
Just short! Short in length and on off, Yash pulls but it goes on one bounce to the fielder inside the ring at mid-wicket.
Goes on the back foot and eases it in the vacant mid-wicket region for a run. 8 from this over.

FOUR! Smacked! Cooper Connolly drags the length short around off, Yash Dhull immediately drops his weight on the back foot and pulls it with all his power to the deep mid-wicket. It races to the fence, beating the full-length dive from a fielder near the boundary line.
200 up for India Under-19! A low full toss, dipping around leg, Rasheed bunts it down to long on for one.
Tossed up and outside off, Yash forces it to sweeper cover for a run.
Flighted and full on off, driven back to the bowler.
Quicker and fuller on middle, Shaik goes down to launch it over the leg side but drags it wide of the keeper. It rolls to short fine leg and they cross.
Another push through the line on the off side and the ball goes to sweeper over. A single to end a 15-run over.
Fuller and around off, slower one, Yash pushes it with gentle hands to covers for a run.
Shortish and outside off, tapped down to cover-point for a single.
FOUR! Make it three in a row and William Salzmann has lost control. Delivers it on a length and outside off, Shaik Rasheed delays his shot and runs it fine down to third man for a boundary.
FOUR! Boom! William Salzmann overpitches this time outside off, Shaik drills it through covers for a cracking boundary.
FOUR! Bang! Short in length and around off, Shaik Rasheed stands tall inside the crease and hammer-pulls it to the deep mid-wicket fence.
Powerplay 3 time. One extra fielder, i.e. 5 can now be put outside the 30-yard circle till the end of this inning. William Salzmann is back into the attack. Can he redeem himself?
Dot ball as this is pushed to cover.
FOUR! Insult to injury! Shorter and outside off. Dhull cracks it away. The man at deep cover runs to his left and slides but cannot stop it.

NO! NO! That is a very poor throw! Should have been a run out there! Short and outside off, Dhull chops it to covers. The batters think of a single for a second and Dhull is down the track, Shaik Rasheed also sets off but then stutters. Dhull is quarter way down the track and should have been run out but William Salzmann throws the ball way, way over the keeper! That allows Dhull to get back in. This is poor from the Aussies. The game is slipping away from them. William Salzmann will have nightmares tonight.
Loopy ball, on off. Dhull taps it to the right of the bowler. Copper gets across and stops it.
Shorter, around off. Dhull punches it towards cover.
Flatter, outside off. Dhull misses the drive.
FOUR! Poor ball and punished! A boundary to start and end the over! Way down the leg side and Shaik Rasheed smacks it to the fine leg fence. 12 from the over!
Again, the ball is nudged towards square leg and the fielder there fails to gather the ball. Easy single.
Darted around off. Shaik flicks it towards square leg for one.

Flatter, lands just outside off and turns back in. Now, Dhull is down on his knees as he is expecting the ball to go on with the angle. He adjusts well and plays it towards short third man for one. An appeal from the keeper but don't know for what!
Loopy ball, on middle, Shaik turns it through square leg for one.

FOUR! You can sense a shift in gears from these two batters! This is tossed up, on off. Shaik Rasheed dances down the track and heaves it wide of the man at long on for a boundary. Pressure on the bowler.
Flatter and wide outside off. This is nicely driven to deep cover for one.
Shorter, around off. Pushed towards backward point.
FOUR! There is no stopping that one! Tossed up, on middle and leg. Shaik Rasheed gets low and nails the sweep shot. The ball races to the square leg fence.
Shorter, around off. Dhull eases it past the diving cover fielder for one.
Shorter and outside off. Rasheed goes back and cuts it to deep point for one.
A full toss, on off. Shaik ends up driving it to short cover.

The heat is taking its toll on the two batsmen. They are having a little break here. Yash Dhull has recently recovered from COVID-19 and this knock will be taking a lot out of him. He is receiving a bit of a back massage from the physio. You can call it an unofficial Drinks break and the umpires are allowing it.
Jack drops it short and outside off, Shaik thrashes it towards deep point for a single.
Another one of the pads and Shaik Rasheed turns it towards backward square leg.
Flatter, outside off. Smacked towards deep cover for one.
Darted on the pads. Dhull looks to flick it away but gets it off his pads towards fine leg. Two leg byes are taken.
Flatter, on off. Tapped to covers for one.
Tossed up, on middle and leg. Dhull goes for the slog-sweep but gets it off the inner half of the bat. It goes towards deep square leg and a single is taken.
Fuller, around off. Dhull strokes it towards long off for yet another single.

FIFTY for Rasheed! Flatter, on off. Rasheed eases it to short cover and sets off for a single. The fielder misses his shy at the bowler's end. The batters have run a bit too far and there is no chance for overthrows. Rasheed now raises his bat towards his dressing room and goes back to work.
Loopy and around off, spinning away, Dhull tries to defend but it takes the outside edge and rolls wide of short third man for a single.
Too full and on off, driven to covers.
Shorter, around off. Dhull chops it to point.
Loopy ball, on off. Worked to long on for one. 150 up.

Collision! The pressure might be getting to the Aussies! Flatter, on middle. It's worked towards mid-wicket and two fielders converge. Nivethan Radhakrishnan rushes across to his left to pick up the ball but Lachlan Shaw comes running across to his right and collides. As a result, Nivethan Radhakrishnan loses the ball and it rolls behind to the deep. A single is taken. Shaw has been really clumsy in the field this morning. Anyway, luckily for Australia, no harm is done to their players.

Short again, but outside off. Dhull smacks it towards cover. It goes aerially but not sure if it carried. The man at cover though dives to his left and gets his hands to it. He half-stops it and the batters take a single.
Jack drops it short, on middle. Dhull rocks back and pulls it wide of deep mid-wicket. The fielder runs to his left and keeps it down to a couple.
Darted on middle and leg. Shaik Rasheed taps it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Shorter, on middle and leg. Punched to deep mid-wicket for one.
Tossed up, lands outside off and turns back in. Shaik tucks it with the spin to square leg for one.
Yet another single as this full ball is worked down to long on.
Shorter, outside off. Shaik rocks back and smacks it past the dive of the man at short cover. The ball goes towards sweeper cover and they get two.
Loopy ball, on off. Blocked out.
Full, on off. Dhull pushes it down the ground. The bowler dives to his left but cannot stop it from going to long off. Single.
A similar shot but Dhull hits it straight to the fielder at cover.
Shorter, around off. Stroked to deep cover for one.

Drinks break. The ongoing partnership between Shaik Rasheed and Yash Dhull has laid a strong platform for India Under-19. They started slowly but in the last few overs, they are picking up the pace. A perfect position to be in for a big finish. Australia Under-19 are looking a bit rattled. It appears that the Indian team took too much out of them with their defensive play and are now taking advantage of some tired bodies. The Aussies need to buck up at the backend otherwise they will end up chasing a massive target. Cooper Connolly is back into the attack after the break.

Single and that brings up the 100-run stand between these two! A really good partnership as India Under-19 were in a precarious situation when these two joined forces. Good recovery and now they would want to take their team to a massive score. Fuller, on off, it's clipped towards deep mid-wicket for an easy single.
Nice and full, just outside off. Shaik plays it with soft hands to cover.
Loopy ball, around off. Blocked away towards point.
Shorter, on off. Dhull pushes it back to the bowler. Jack Sinfield dives to his right but fumbles. Single taken.
Loopy ball, on off. Tucked to mid-wicket.
Shorter, down the leg side. Dhull misses the flick. Wide called.
Jack Sinfield has not started his second spell well. Gone for a boundary on the first ball, pressure on him...

FOUR! Beats mid off! Jack Sinfield comes 'round the stumps and bowls it full and outside off, Dhull smashes it down the ground. The man at mid off dives to his right but cannot stop the ball. It runs away to the fence.
Short and outside off again. This is cut away wide of sweeper cover for a couple. 10 from the over India Under-19 could look to get a move on now.

Good running! Length ball, on off. Dhull taps it towards mid on and sets off for a single. The fielder runs to his left and moves forward to get to the ball. He underarms it at the bowler's end but misses the stumps.
Shorter and outside off. Shaik Rasheed chops it to sweeper cover for one.
On a length but still wide outside off. Eased down to third man for one.
FOUR! Nope, you cannot afford to bowl there! William Salzmann bowls it short and wide outside off. Dhull frees his arms and thrashes it to the backward point fence.
Shorter, outside off. Shaik Rasheed looks to punch it away but gets it off the toe end. The ball races away to third man for one.
William Salzmann is back into the attack. 1/24 in his 5 overs so far.
Quick single. Length ball, on off. Shaik pushes it to mid off and sets off for a single. The fielder is right at the edge of the circle so the batters get the single with ease.
Shorter, around off. Dhull cuts it to third man for one.

FOUR! That is a top shot! Yash Dhull brings up his 50 with a great shot! Whitney digs it short, around off. This doesn't bounce too much but Dhull gets under it and plays the short-arm jab to the mid-wicket fence. One bounce and over the ropes. He raises the bat towards his teammates and goes back to work. His job is still not done.
A similar delivery but this time Dhull plays it back to the bowler.
Length ball again, right on the off pole. Dhull pushes it to covers.
On a length, on middle and leg. Dhull blocks it towards mid on.
Short again, outside off, Yash Dhull goes back and smashes it to the right of the fielder at deep cover. Just a single.
Slower through the air, short and outside off, Yash goes back and cuts it to deep point. Good placement and they earn two runs.
Fullish and on off, Shaik drives it a bit straighter this time and sends it down to long off for a run.
Very full and on middle, Shaik drives this time but finds the cover fielder.
Flighted and full outside off, Dhull drives it through mid off and collects a single.
Nivethan Radhakrishnan bowls left-arm this time, a full toss on middle, Shaik eases it down to long on for a single.
Fuller this time, around off, Yash drives but again picks out the same cover fielder.
Shortish and on off, Dhull punches off the back foot but finds the cover fielder.
Quick run. Tom delivers it around off, Shaik drops it with gentle hands to covers and steals a run. Great thinking.
Hangs on the back foot and forces a length ball to cover-point for one.

On a length around off, it's tapped down to the left of the cover fielder. They cross for a run as the fielder has a shy at the striker's end. No one is backing up the throw and they take another run.
FOUR! A gentle loosener from Tom Whitney, short and wide outside off, Yash Dhull rocks back and smacks it through point for a cracking boundary.
Tom Whitney (5-0-15-0) is brought back on.
Three runs. A touch short again, around off, Yash Dhull plays very late, almost off the keeper's gloves and guides towards third man. This pair is slowly picking up the pace. 100 up!
Short and outside off, cut through point for a couple of runs.

Direct hit at the keeper's end but the onfield umpire has turned down the appeal straightaway. Loopy and full around leg, Shaik Rasheed flicks it in front of square leg and they cross for a quick run. Teague Wyllie picks up the ball and scores a direct hit but Yash Dhull is safe. The replays show that Yash took it easy initially and then had to rush.
Allows the ball to spin back in and hits it firmly to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Flatter off spinner, it's punched off the back foot to mid on.
Full and floated outside off, driven through the line but straight to the cover fielder.
Change in bowling. Nivethan Radhakrishnan has been brought on now.
Tossed up, full and on off, the batsman is forward in defense. They are rushing through their overs.
Around the pads, it's helped to square leg, not in the gap.
Floated and on middle, Shaik forces it down towards mid on and this time the mid-wicket fielder makes a clean stop to his left.
Full and on middle, Dhull pushes it down towards mid on. The mid-wicket fielder dives across to his left but doesn't make a clean stop and concedes a single.
Advances down the track and wrists it down to long on for a single.
Fires a full ball on the pads, Yash tucks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Skidding down the leg side, Yash Dhull nudges it behind square leg for a run.
Fullish and outside off, pushed down to long off for a single.

Beautiful delivery! Cooper Connolly bowls it flat and around off, it lands and spins away square to beat Shaik Rasheed's hanging defensive bat. The keeper collects it and breaks the stumps but Shaik has never left the crease.
Fullish and around off, skidding in, Dhull drives it square of the wicket on the off side and jogs across to the other end.
Arm ball, around off, pushed from the back foot towards the bowler.
The 50-run stand comes up, off 79 balls! Short and outside off, eased down to long off for a single.
Flatter and shorter on off, Yash goes on the back foot and punches it towards the bowler. India Under-19 are 86/2 at the halfway mark.
Uses the spin and tucks it in front of square leg. They cross for a single.
Flatter and quicker on off, forced past the diving mid-wicket fielder for a single.

FOUR! Excellent late adjustment! Slightly short and outside off, Yash Dhull shapes up to play the square cut but the ball bounces more than he expected. The skipper does well eventually to play late and dabs it down to third man for a boundary.
Tossed up, on middle, worked towards mid-wicket for an easy run.
Presses forward to a full ball and pushes it defensively back to the bowler.
Fuller and on off, driven through the line and Cooper Connolly rushes across to his left to collect the ball.
Arm ball on middle, a bit on the shorter side, Dhull punches from the crease to short cover.
Loopy and full on off, Yash Dhull offers a straight bat in defense.
Very full and on middle, helped out to mid-wicket.
Fuller on off, the batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Fuller and on middle, knocked down to long on for a single.

DROPPED! Could be a costly miss by Shaw. Slower through the air, full and around off. It turns back in slowly off the surface and Shaik Rasheed flicks it aerially towards mid-wicket. Lachlan Shaw jumps but fails to hold on to the catch over his head. They cross for a run.
Plays it with the spin and nudges it in front of square leg for a run.
Full and flighted outside off, it's driven firmly but straight to the fielder at covers. He fumbles but no run is taken.
Uses his feet to come down the track and strokes a full ball down to long off for a single.
Slower through the air, full and on off, Rasheed is forward as he defends it on the leg side.
Slightly short and outside off, Dhull rocks back and cuts it to deep point for a single.
Drags his length short and Dhull forces it to sweeper cover for another run in this over.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Short and outside off, Shaik Rasheed goes back and cuts it to deep point for a single.
Floated and on off, tapped down to covers for a quick run.
Tossed up, full and on off, defended back off the front foot.
FOUR! Poor delivery, short and wide outside off, Yash Dhull goes on the back foot and whacks it to the deep cover fence.
Fuller and around off, it's defended off the front foot to the off side.
Strides forward and drives it back. Jack Sinfield goes down low to his right to make the stop.
A touch short and on off, Yash Dhull stands back and punches it through mid-wicket for a single.
Flatter and on middle, defended back.
Loopy and full around off, defended off the front foot.

Was that edged? Looks more like bat and pad, than an outside edge. Full and floated outside off, going straight on, Yash Dhull presses forward to defend but it whizzes past the outside edge. The keeper fails to gather it.
A single to end the over. On, off and Dhull plays it towards long off for one.
Loopy ball, on off. Blocked out.
A bit shorter and quicker, outside off. Shaik Rasheed nicely drives it to sweeper cover for one.
Tossed up, right in the line of the off pole. Shaik Rasheed blocks it under his eyes.
Very full by the bowler, around off. Dhull punches it to long off for one.
Loopy ball, on off. Blocked back towards the bowler.
Well played. Shorter, lands outside off and turns back in. Dhull stays back, lets the ball turn and then plays it past short third man. The batters get one.
Nicely bowled. Loopy ball, just outside off. But Dhull responds with a good defence off the front foot.
Just a single as this flatter ball is punched to long off.
Loopy ball, outside off. A nice stride and Shaik Rasheed blocks it to covers.
FOUR! Poor ball and gets the treatment! Short and down the leg side. Shaik Rasheed rocks back and pulls it over the man at backward square leg for a boundary.
Tossed-up delivery, outside off. Shaik Rasheed puts a nice stride in to block it.
Loopy ball, around off. Shaik Rasheed flicks it past mid-wicket for one.
Fuller, just outside off. Punched towards covers.
Fired full, on the pads. Worked to mid-wicket.
Yet another single as Dhull punches it to the right of the bowler. Cooper dives there but cannot stop it from going to long on.
Flatter, around off. Played past backward point for one.
Fuller, on off. Pushed back to the bowler. The ball hits the bowler's hands and goes to long off. Single for Dhull.
Another change in bowling. Skipper Cooper Connolly brings himself into the attack. He bowls useful left-arm orthodox spin and has done a decent job in the tournament so far.
Loopy ball, on off. Pushed to covers. Should have been a maiden but this is a good start for Jack Sinfield.
Misfield! Loopy ball, on middle and leg. Shaik Rasheed works it away and the man at backward square leg fumbles. It goes towards the ropes and they get two.
Flatter, on off, tucked to the leg side with the spin.
Loopy ball, on off, it's pushed down the ground but the man at mid on dives to his left to stop it.
Flatter, on off. Shaik helps it to mid-wicket.
Tossed up, around off. Worked towards the leg side. Dot ball.

Change in bowling. Spin for the first time, Jack Sinfield is ready to roll his arm. A slight hold-up in play and the reason is that Jack Nisbet, who had gone off the field, wants to join back. The umpire lets him in and off goes Aidan Cahill.
Back of a length, around off. Dhull plays it to point again but this time they do not attempt a quick single.

On a length, on off. It's tapped wide of point and Dhull sets off for a single. The fielder hits the stumps at the bowler's end and then the ball deflects towards deep mid-wicket. The fielder there has to chase it and the batters take the second.
On a length, just outside off. Dhull taps it to point and follows it with a loud 'NO' to stop his partner.
Length ball, on middle. Shaik shuffles across and looks to flick it away. The ball hits his pads and rolls towards square leg. A leg bye then.
Shorter, around off. Punched by Dhull. The man at point dives to his right but cannot stop it. Single.
Length ball, on off. Worked past mid-wicket for one.
Tap and run. Shaik Rasheed taps this length ball towards point and they set off for a quick single.
Short of a length, outside off. Dhull pushes it towards sweeper cover for one.
Another wide! One more bumper and Dhull lets the ball sail over him. Wide called again.
Wide! A bumper, on off. Dhull lets it sail over his head and the umpire calls it a wide. A tennis-ball bounce on that.
Back of a length, around off. Tapped to point.
Back of a length, on middle, Shaik Rasheed shuffles across and tickles it to fine leg for one.
Full and wide enough for the batter to leave it with ease.
Shorter, around off. Shaik Rasheed rises and blocks it to covers.

Drinks break. Very slow going from India Under-19, perhaps they already have assessed the conditions and have a target in mind. That said, two wickets have gone down and the current run rate could be bothering them slightly. Australia Under-19 won't mind India's approach much, runs are not flowing and if they keep on picking wickets at regular intervals, that will help them in maintaining the upper hand.  A very important middle phase coming our way now. Jack Nisbet to continue after the break...
On a length, wide outside off. Dhull gets bat on it as he cuts but the man at backward point dives to his left and stops it.
Beaten again! This lands outside off, on a length and comes back in. Dhull looks to block it away from his body but it goes past the outside edge.
Beaten! Very well bowled. Length ball, outside off and shaping away. Dhull has a tentative push but is beaten.

Great effort in the deep! Short and wide outside off. Dhull latches onto it and cuts it towards deep point. Campbell Kellaway runs to his left and dives to stop the ball. The TV umpire checks it and is happy with Kellaway's effort. Two runs saved.
Full ball, just outside off. Dhull blocks it to cover.
Length ball, on middle and leg. Worked towards square leg for one.
Shorter, on off. Dhull gets on top of the bounce to block it.  A successful over for Jack Nisbet.
Length but down the leg side. Dhull misses the flick shot. Wide called.
On a length, around off. Dhull blocks it to the off side.
Length ball, around off. Tapped out from the crease.
Skipper Yash Dhull walks in next.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Just the second wicket for Jack Nisbet in the tournament and this is a big one! India Under-19 slide further as they have lost both their openers. A lucky break for the Aussies though. Short and down the leg side. Harnoor Singh goes for the pull but gets a faint tickle on it off the gloves. Tobias Snell gathers the ball and they are celebrating. Up goes the finger and Harnoor Singh walks back to the hut.
Commentary.Howout: c Tobias Snell b Jack Nisbet

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on the pads. Singh looks to work it away to the leg side but closes the face of the bat early. It takes the leading edge and rolls away safely to covers.
Length ball, on off. Tapped wide of mid-wicket for a single. There is a direct hit at the keeper's end and the ball rolls away towards cover but the batters don't attempt to take the extra run.
Full ball, outside off. Singh looks to whip it away to the leg side but gets an inside edge on the pads.
Shorter and wider again, this time Shaik Rasheed punches it to sweeper cover for one.
Back of a length, around off. Tapped towards backward point.
On a length, on middle and leg. Blocked out.
Too full and wide outside off. Singh opens the face of the bat and drives it past the diving point fielder. The man in the deep runs across and keeps it to a single.
Full ball, angling across off. Singh stays in the crease to block it out.
A maiden for Jack Nisbet then. Back of a length, around off. Punched towards short cover.
Nice and full, outside off. Shaik Rasheed puts in a nice stride to block it.
Very full, around off. Pushed towards mid on by Shaik.
Even better this time! Back of a length, on off. Shaik Rasheed taps it out to the off side, looks for a quick single, but Harnoor Singh sends him back.
Better. Length ball, closer to the stumps. Shaik pushes it towards backward point.
Nisbet bowls it shorter outside off. Rasheed leaves it with ease though.
Powerplay 2 time. A maximum of 4 fielders are now allowed outside the ring till the 40th over. There is a bowling change now. Jack Nisbet is back on, replacing Tom Whitney.

FOUR! Beautifully picked up off the pads! William Salzmann serves it very full around middle and leg, the angle is taking it further down, Harnoor Singh leans across stylishly and flicks it over backward square leg for a boundary. 11 from the over, a good finish to Powerplay 1 from India Under-19.
Wide! Sliding down the leg side, on a length, Harnoor fails to buy some cheap runs as he misses to get some bat behind it.
FOUR! That's a classy shot! William Salzmann angles in a length ball around off, Harnoor Singh presses forward and creams his drive through the gap at extra cover. Sublime.
Goes short and wide outside off, Singh stands tall and plays it down to the cover-point region.
Back of a length, on middle, Singh goes back and taps it down in front of square leg.
This one is too full in length, around off and angling in, Harnoor Singh leans forward and across before flicking it in the gap at mid-wicket. Two runs added to the scoreboard.
Hurls it across on a length outside off, Harnoor Singh allows it through to the keeper.
Tom Whitney keeps it full and on off, Shaik Rasheed attempts to play straight but the face of the bat closes slightly and he ends up helping it towards mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, Rasheed lunges and defends it right under his watchful eyes.
FOUR! Quality shot! Too full in length and around off, Shaik Rasheed gets forward with a vertical bat, shows a high front elbow and lifts it behind the bowler's head for a boundary.
Wide! Reload. Tom Whitney lets off a grunt as he digs it in short. But the line is down the leg side and it's an easy leave for Shaik.
Bowls it full and outside off, angling in a shade, Rasheed takes a little stride forward to cover the line as he shoulders arms.
Pitches it just behind the fuller length, around off, Shaik Rasheed strides forward and offers a solid defensive shot.
Back of a length around off, some extra bounce, Shaik goes back and defends it from the inner portion of his bat.

This one is delivered on a driving length outside off, inviting the batsman, Harnoor Singh strides forward and leaves it alone. That was just flirting with the tram line. End of a successful over for William Salzmann.
On a good length, around middle and leg, Shaik Rasheed works it behind square leg and opens his account with a single.
Wide! Short in length but way wide outside off, it's left alone by Shaik Rasheed.
Shaik Rasheed is the next batter. India Under-19 need a bit more tempo in this game now.

OUT! The off stump goes for a walk! William Salzmann gets his line right and provides Australia Under-19 with their first breakthrough. It's a gem of a delivery. Salzmann goes wide of the crease and angles it on a length around off. Angkrish Raghuvanshi tries to defend the line but it straightens just a hint to beat his bat and uproot the off stump. William Salzmann is happy as Angkrish Raghuvanshi departs for a 30-ball 6.
Back of a length, outside off, Angkrish Raghuvanshi goes on the back foot but plays a mistimed square cut to point.

Wide! That's a tempter from William Salzmann. Pitches it up on a driving length but the line is quite wide, Angkrish allows it through. There was some movement off the surface and all William needs to do is to get his line right.
In the channel outside off, on a length and holding its line, Raghuvanshi shoulders arms.
Starts his spell with a delivery on a length, around off and angling in, Angkrish Raghuvanshi plays late and taps it down towards point.
First bowling change of the game. William Salzmann is set to bowl now.
Pitches it up and outside off, Harnoor presses forward and pushes it towards mid off. Once again his bat closed at the point of contact. 15 runs after 7 overs, very quiet going from India Under-19!
Serves it on a good length around off, Harnoor Singh goes on the back foot and blocks it towards mid on.
Lands it on a length and just outside off, Angkrish Raghuvanshi plays late and guides it down to third man for a single.
Angling in from around off, Raghuvanshi helps it off his pads to square leg.

Swing and a miss! Angkrish Raghuvanshi loses his composure and attempts for a massive shot down the ground. He misses and Tom Whitney has a few words to fire at the batter. On a length and outside off, Angkrish Raghuvanshi goes for an expansive drive but fails to connect.
Hurls it on a length close to off, angling in, Angkrish Raghuvanshi remains on the back foot and defends it close to his body.
On a good length around off, Harnoor Singh commits himself on the front foot and defends it to the off side. Tidy over.
Wide! This one is quite wide outside off, it's left alone by Singh and the umpire stretches his arms.
Good carry to the keeper this time. On a length around off, angling across the left-hander, Harnoor shoulders arms and Tobias Snell collects it in front of his face.
A touch short in length and outside off, Harnoor Singh hangs on the back foot and lets it through to the keeper.
Identical to the last delivery, again the line is not close enough to make the batter play. A simple leave.
In the channel outside off, left alone by Singh.

EDGED BUT SAFE! Jack Nisbet delivers it around middle and off and gets it to shape away from there, Harnoor Singh is compelled to play that line as he tries to defend. But the ball moves away to take the outside edge. Luckily for Singh, it doesn't carry to the second slip fielder.

Too full in length, around off, Singh tries to play it across but his bat turns in his hands and the ball dribbles wide of mid on. They cross for a single. A steady going from India, they have not shown the intent to go after the bowlers.
Width there outside off, short in length, Angkrish Raghuvanshi reaches out and cuts it down to third man for a single.
Lands it full and on off, Angkrish brings down a straight bat and drives it straight back to the bowler.
Pitches it up and around middle, Angkrish Raghuvanshi plays an on drive but fails to find the gap.
Wide! Tom Whitney tries to go short but fails to control his line, it starts from leg and goes down the leg side, Angkrish allows it through.

Misses out. Fuller and around off, angling in, Angkrish Raghuvanshi flicks it across the line but finds the fielder inside the ring at mid-wicket. Either side of that fielder and that would have been a boundary.
A touch short in length and outside off, Angkrish Raghuvanshi camps back and forces it through the line. He finds the point fielder.
Around off, on a length, Harnoor Singh goes on the back foot and defends it to the off side.
The line is quite straight on this occasion, Raghuvanshi eases it behind square leg, to the right of the fielder stationed there, and it's an easy single.
Delivers it on a length around off, Angkrish tries to defend it from the front foot but it nips back in slightly to take the inner edge. It goes to square leg.

Controlled edge! Jack Nisbet serves it on a length and outside off, Angkrish Raghuvanshi remains on the back foot as he opens the face of his bat late. It takes a soft outside edge and rolls in front of the slip cordon.
A low dipping full ball, around off, Angkrish is forward and brings his bat down in time to keep it out towards mid on.
Angling in from a length around off, Angkrish Raghuvanshi stays back and defends it close to his body.
Fuller and around off, Harnoor gets on the front foot and works it towards mid-wicket as his bottom hand comes off the handle. It's been a decent start from both teams.
FOUR! First boundary of the match! A leg-stump half volley, Harnoor Singh leans across stylishly and flicks it past the left side of the square leg umpire for a glorious boundary.
Easy leave. This one is on a driving length outside off, shaping away, Singh has nothing to do with it.
Fuller and around off, Harnoor Singh leans forward and closes the face of his bat a bit as he bunts it down to mid on.
Good length, around off and shaping away again, Harnoor covers his stumps and allows it through.

First ball faced by Harnoor Singh and he gets beaten comprehensively. Tom Whitney serves it on a length around leg, shaping away, Singh tries to defend it from the back foot but misses. The keeper collects it very low.
On a length and outside off, Angkrish Raghuvanshi opens the face of his bat and pushes it to the right of the second slip fielder. He moves across quickly and stops the ball.

A muted appeal for an lbw, turned down. Fuller and closer to off, angling in, Angkrish Raghuvanshi strides forward and brings his bat and pad close in defense. The bowler appeals thinking that it's pad first but the umpire shakes his head.
Gets on the front foot and drives it through the line, finds the cover fielder.

Jack Nisbet is trying to overcompensate his line after getting driven once. Around middle and leg, angling down, Angkrish fails to flick again and this time it clips his pads before rolling away to the keeper.

Appeal for a caught behind but the umpire signals a WIDE! A length ball, sliding down the leg side, Angkrish Raghuvanshi tries to flick but fails to middle his shot. The keeper and the slip cordon go up in an appeal but there is nothing from the umpire. No bat.
Slightly overpitched on this occasion, around off, Angkrish Raghuvanshi gets on the front foot and caresses it through the gap at covers. He picks up a couple of runs.
Right on the button. Fuller and around off, Angkrish Raghuvanshi presses forward and defends it down towards mid on.
Jack Nisbet will use the other new ball.
First run from the bat! This delivery starts from middle and angles down, Angkrish Raghuvanshi clips it down to fine leg and opens his account.
Full in length, around off and angling in, Angkrish Raghuvanshi plays it in front of his pads and pushes it gently towards mid on.
Another delivery in the region outside off, the batsman shoulders arms.
Slightly full this time, outside off, Raghuvanshi takes a little stride forward to cover his stumps and then makes a leave.
Gets his line right on this occasion. Tom Whitney serves it on a length and in the zone outside off, the batter drops his wrists and offers no shot.
Wide! Wrong line from Tom Whitney. Delivers it on a good length around middle and off and it angles down the leg side. Angkrish gets across the stumps and lets it be.

Some extra bounce straightaway. A touch short in length and close to off, Angkrish Raghuvanshi goes on his toes and does well to defend it with a loose bottom hand. The ball comes off the upper half of his bat and rolls to backward point.

All in readiness. The boys concerned are out in the middle. Angkrish Raghuvanshi and Harnoor Singh are the openers for India Under-19. Clear blue skies here at the moment but the early morning conditions will offer something to the pacers. The start is going to be very critical. Tom Whitney is marking his run-up and is getting ready to bowl the first over. Let's play...

The players from both sides walk out to the middle. First things first, they will line up for their respective national anthems. All the players looking very calm but there will be a storm going on in their bellies. Big pressure game.

Australia Under-19 (Playing XI) - Campbell Kellaway, Teague Wyllie, Corey Miller, Cooper Connolly (C), Lachlan Shaw, Nivethan Radhakrishnan (In for Aidan Cahill), William Salzmann, Tobias Snell (WK), Jack Sinfield, Tom Whitney, Jack Nisbet.

India Under-19 (Playing XI) - Angkrish Raghuvanshi, Harnoor Singh, Shaik Rasheed, Yash Dhull (C), Raj Angad Bawa, Nishant Sindhu (In for Siddharth Yadav), Kaushal Tambe, Dinesh Bana (WK), Rajvardhan Hangargekar, Vicky Ostwal, Ravi Kumar.
Toss - Up goes the coin and it comes down in favour of Yash Dhull. India Under-19 elect to bat!
TOSS - The news from the middle is that the coin has landed in favour of India Under-19. They have chosen to BAT first!

Did you know? India U-19 have bowled out all four of their opponents so far in this edition and have scored 300 twice, which included a gigantic 405 against Uganda U-19. Needless to say, Australia U-19 have their task cut out.

Both the teams have had a great tournament so far. India Under-19 are yet to lose a single match while Australia Under-19 have lost just one match back in the group stage. Moreover, the Indian side has been bolstered by the return of its key players who were out due to Covid-19 and that will only add to the excitement of this clash. The last two times these two teams met in a knockout match of the Under-19 World Cup, it was the team from India that emerged victorious. They won the final of the tournament held in 2018 against Australia Under-19 and in the quarter-final of the 2020 Under-19 World Cup, the Indian boys defeated the Australians by 74 runs to knock them out. The Aussies will be keen to settle the scores but it is not going to be easy against this quality side. Stay tuned for the toss and team news.

Hello and a very warm welcome to one of the most highly-anticipated clashes of the Under-19 World Cup. India Under-19 will face Australia Under-19 in the second semi-final and the winner of the clash will face England Under-19 in the final. Both these countries are powerhouses when it comes to cricket talent and that has been quite evident with their show so far in the Under-19 World Cup, this should be a cracker of a clash but there can be only one winner. Will the team from India move forward to play in the final? Or will the Australian's take on their age-old rivals in the final on 5th February. Stay with us to find out.
